correctness.rationale: Johnson shortest-path exchange proves exactly the rank-k Boolean intervals are geodesically convex. For each support, convex-hull separation yields the (known) private-one/private-zero witness criterion. Disjoint selected witnesses of mixed types imply p≤n−k−1, q≤k−1; pure types imply the rank-based bounds. Explicit P/Q/R supports attain the upper bound. In the mixed maximum case all inequalities are equalities; the column-incidence multiplicities 1,q,t−1 uniquely recover P,Q,R. The pure-boundary exceptions are counted separately. The standalone checker directly compares graph convexity and interval sets on J(3,1), J(4,2), J(5,2), checks 21,700 support traces in J(6,3), exhaustively counts all maxima for n≤7, and validates larger constructions. Infinite result is mathematical proof, not finite extrapolation. No outstanding correctness gap identified.

value.rationale: Extremal size and cardinality profile of shattered supports are intrinsic invariants of a graph-geodesic concept class. The all-rank formula identifies a sharp VC-dimension plateau, exceptional rank-two and rank-three regimes, a complete canonical partition classification, and an exact multinomial plus boundary correction for every finite Johnson graph. These determine the full set of maximum shattered supports, not merely reproduce a known box membership test. No unproved downstream results are asserted.
